nodes.name: Oaks (white oak and relatives)
nodes.desc: The dominant upland trees. The MDC lists white oak acorns as food for turkeys, deer, squirrels, jays, raccoons and mice, with acorns ripening in autumn.

nodes.name: Glade grasses & wildflowers
nodes.desc: Plants of open, rocky, sun-baked glades where the soil is thin and trees are few. Fire management helps keep glades open.

nodes.name: Stream algae & aquatic plants
nodes.desc: Algae on rocks and plants in clear, cool spring-fed streams grow the food that aquatic insects and crayfish graze.

nodes.name: White-tailed deer
nodes.desc: Eats leaves, twigs, fruits and nuts of trees and shrubs and the foliage of herbs, per the MDC. Coyotes and bobcats prey on it.

nodes.name: Wild turkey
nodes.desc: Leans on hard mast such as acorns in fall and winter and on insects in summer. Poults depend almost entirely on insects for their first month.

nodes.name: Eastern gray squirrel
nodes.desc: A nut-eater that harvests acorns and hickory nuts in the oak-hickory forest and is prey for bobcats and coyotes.

nodes.name: Grasshoppers
nodes.desc: Chew glade grasses and wildflowers. The MDC lists grasshoppers as food for collared lizards, and turkeys eat insects too.

nodes.name: Aquatic insects
nodes.desc: Larvae graze algae in clear streams. Adults hatch into the air, where gray bats and fish catch them.

nodes.name: Crayfish
nodes.desc: Scavenging omnivores of stream bottoms. The MDC says crayfish are the main food of Ozark hellbenders and are eaten by smallmouth bass.

nodes.name: Bobcat
nodes.desc: Stalks rabbits, squirrels, turkeys and deer fawns. The MDC names bobcats as deer predators.

nodes.name: Eastern collared lizard
nodes.desc: Lives on sunny, rocky glades and eats grasshoppers, beetles, spiders and even small lizards and snakes. Snakes and hawks prey on it.

nodes.name: Gray bat
nodes.desc: Roosts in caves and hunts night-flying insects, many with aquatic larvae, over streams and reservoirs. Depends on a few cold winter caves and warmer summer caves.

nodes.name: Smallmouth bass
nodes.desc: Cool, clear Ozark streams with rock or gravel bottoms. Eats minnows, crayfish and large aquatic insects, and its eggs and fry are eaten by sunfish.

nodes.name: Ozark hellbender
nodes.desc: A big aquatic salamander of cool, rocky rivers in the White and Black river systems. Mostly eats crayfish. Silt, disease and poor water quality are threats.

nodes.name: American black bear
nodes.desc: Omnivore that fattens on acorns in late fall and also eats plants, insects, fawns and carrion. Once nearly eliminated from Missouri but now growing.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: A flexible predator. The MDC names coyotes among animals that kill deer, and it also takes turkeys and squirrels.

nodes.name: Northern river otter
nodes.desc: Fish are the main food and crayfish a close second, per Wikipedia. Hunts the streams and rivers.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Powers the forest canopy, glade plants and stream algae.

nodes.name: Rainfall
nodes.desc: Feeds the forest and, by soaking into limestone, the springs and streams.

nodes.name: Fire
nodes.desc: The NPS says fire management helps collared lizards and turkeys by keeping glades and woodlands open.

nodes.name: Spring-fed water
nodes.desc: Springs keep Ozark streams cool and clear year round, the habitat that hellbenders and smallmouth bass need.

nodes.name: Thin rocky soil
nodes.desc: Limestone and chert soils hold the oak-hickory forest; glade soils are especially thin.

nodes.name: Fungi, insects & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down leaf litter and dead animals and return nutrients to the soil.
